verdict.rationale: Codex lets users decide which external tools it can reach: they add or remove local and remote MCP servers via `codex mcp add`, inspect each session's available tools before Codex uses them, and opt into live web search per run with `--search`. These are per-user configuration choices, not admin-enforced governance. The evidence shows no organization-level allowlist or denylist for integrations, no per-tool enable/disable inside a server, and no central policy an engineering lead could push to a team (the RBAC doc covers the OpenAI API platform, not Codex integrations). missing for 10: org/admin-enforced integration allowlists, per-tool allow/deny controls, centrally managed policy across team members, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can control which external tools and integrations the agent is allowed to access

citations.quote: Add local or remote MCP servers, authenticate when needed, and inspect the tools available to the current session before Codex uses them.
In the `codex` TUI, use `/mcp` to see your active MCP servers.
Switch a run to live web search when a task depends on current releases, documentation, or external behavior.
Choose the model, reasoning effort, permissions, and commands that fit the task.
